chunks: He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Muqri reported to me from Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Asadi, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Abdillah al-Alawi, from Yahya ibn Hashim al-Ghassani, from Abu al-Muqawwam Yahya ibn Tha'labah al-Ansari, from Asim ibn Abu al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said:

We were with the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, on one of his journeys when a Bedouin shouted at us with a loud voice: 'O Muhammad!' The Prophet said: 'What do you want?' He said: 'What about a person who loves a people but does not follow their deeds?' The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: 'A person is with whom he loves.' Then he said: 'O Muhammad, present Islam to me.' He said: 'Testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer, give the zakat, fast the month of Ramadan, and perform pilgrimage to the House.'

He said: 'O Muhammad, do you take any reward for this?' He said: 'No, except the love for the near kin.' He asked: 'My kin or your kin?' He said: 'Rather, my kin.' He said: 'Extend your hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you. There is no good in one who does not love you and does not love your kinsfolk.'

key_terms.أبايعك: Bay’ah — the pledge of allegiance, a formal act of accepting authority
key_terms.المرء مع من أحب: A person is with whom he loves — a famous Prophetic saying indicating spiritual companionship through love
key_terms.المودة في القربى: Love for the near kin — a Quranic concept (42:23) interpreted in Shia tradition as love for the Prophet’s family (Ahlulbayt)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the reward for accepting Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration, a Bedouin approaches the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) during a journey and asks whether a person who loves a people but does not follow their practices can still be counted among them. The Prophet replies with the famous dictum: ‘A person is with whom he loves.’ The Bedouin then asks the Prophet to present Islam to him, and after hearing the pillars, inquires about any payment. The Prophet states the only reward he asks is love for his near kin (Ahlulbayt), referencing Quran 42:23. The Bedouin, upon learning this, willingly pledges allegiance and affirms that there is no good in anyone who does not love the Prophet and his family.
